305	### The Wet-Hay Theory (Refuted)
306	Argument: wet hay of Hessel Bottom thinned the cream
307	- State Agricultural College Bulletin No. 214 tested this (1911)
308	- Result: bog hay depressed butterfat by at most 5 hundredths in winter, nothing measurable in summer
309	- Gap was 19 hundredths year-round, July and February alike
310	- Verdict: four times too small and wrong shape

312	### Bulletin No. 471 Conclusion
313	Published October 1958, co-authored by Ivy Keddie and Professor Vaught:
314	> No milk was watered at Ostrey Hollow and no cream was stolen there. From the first of May, 1897, to the twelfth of June, 1923, the station's tests were low by one part in twenty because its pipettes were short by one part in twenty, and the difference — seventy-six thousand pounds of butter fat — stands credited in the Association's own ledgers, year by year, as station gain.

324	## Wilbur Teague's Bookkeeper Testimony (Retelling 05, 1948 memoir)
325	
326	### The Station-Gain Account (Invented 1905)
327	Teague created the "station-gain" line to track accounting reality:
328	- One side: butterfat credited to patrons on station's test (what the station books said it bought)
329	- Other side: butterfat actually received at Larrow Green in cream (what they actually had)
330	- The second was always larger by 5.25 percent
331	
332	**1898 entry (example):**
333	- Credited to patrons: 57,760 lb
334	- Received at Larrow Green: 60,800 lb
335	- Station gain: 3,040 lb (five and a quarter percent)
336	- Entry phrase: "as usual" (which stopped anyone looking)
337	
338	**Why invented:** "A difference that will not be entered somewhere will come back and bite you at audit"
339	
340	### Teague's Theory on Arrangement
341	Testimony to board of arbitration (and repeated in 1948):
342	> Cream is portable, and that station was in one pair of hands for twenty-nine seasons. One man weighed the milk, one man drew the sample, one man made the test, one man wrote the figure that the pay slip was made from, and one man ran the separator. There was no second man in that building from the spring to the fall. I do not say what any particular person did on any particular day, because I was not there and I do not know. I say that a business which is arranged so that a single man can take a little and write down a little less is a business that will sooner or later have a little taken from it, and that no set of books ever made can prevent it. The remedy is two men or a lock, and the Association had neither.
343	
344	### Teague's 1916 Warning
345	- Put the discrepancy to Selby Vose in 1916
346	- Was told to "let it alone"
347	- Complied; was not the Association's conscience
348	- A bookkeeper who takes business up twice after being told once "has generally begun to look for another employer"

355	- One break in the pattern: spring 1911 (measure replacement) — recorded as "small charge for replacement and nothing else"

626	## Leland Vaught's Bulletin No. 471 Introduction (October 1958)
627	
628	**Provides technical and scientific proof of pipette defect:**
629	- Question posed: why did milk from one skimming station run below creamery 7 miles down same valley for 50 years?
630	- Answer: "a piece of glass" — the milk pipette
631	- Key principle: milk pipette is instrument in butterfat test which plant cannot check against anything; it is instrument on which every figure in plant depends
632	- Standard charge: 17.6 cubic centimeters
633	- If pipette delivers less than mark: less milk → less fat → shorter column → reading low in exact proportion charge was short
